structure: One ruling file, workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-sam-2026-11-17.md, 20 lines in four pieces: a two-line preamble saying the ruling was given in the overview-and-review build session, answers the review page's wording question (where the prototype names one thing two ways), and replaces the 16 November orchestrator decision to take each question page's own wording; a numbered list of three decisions (1 the exit port, 2 the arrival date, 3 addresses, whose third item carries three sub-bullets for section heading, heading/H1/task row/card title, and validation message); Sam's verbatim words as one quoted paragraph, which is the source the three listed decisions are read from; and a closing two-line paragraph of orchestrator's calls applying the ruling (section numbers stay, the overview row's hint stays, plants takes the same address wording because plants matches animals on these pages). The scope is the whole file, so nothing is left out; the file names no page file, no component and no repo path, and gives no wording for anything beyond the exit port, the arrival date and the addresses section, so it settles only those three wording points and the three applying calls.

parts.title: The whole ruling: review-page wording for exit port, arrival date and addresses
parts.scope: The entire file, every line of it: the preamble, all three numbered decisions with the three sub-bullets under decision 3, Sam's verbatim quoted words, and the closing orchestrator's calls. Nothing in this source belongs to another part.
covers: Decision 1: the exit port is "Port of exit" everywhere, check your answers included, and "Exit border control post" is not used — one claim for the wording to use, and the rejected wording recorded with it or as its own claim.
Decision 2: the arrival date is "Arrival date at port of entry" everywhere, check your answers included, and "Arrival date at destination" is not used — the wording to use and the rejected wording.

Decision 3: addresses read the same on check your answers, the overview (task list) and the addresses page itself, with its three sub-bullets each claimed: section heading "Addresses"; heading (H1, task row and card title) "Consignment addresses"; validation, the incomplete-card message, "Complete consignment addresses".

The preamble's two framing facts: the ruling answers the review page's wording question where the prototype names one thing two ways, and it replaces the 16 November orchestrator decision to take each question page's own wording — so the earlier decision no longer stands.

The three orchestrator's calls applying the ruling: section numbers stay ("5. Addresses"); the overview row's hint stays; plants takes the same address wording, since plants matches animals on these pages.

Every listed decision checked word for word against Sam's verbatim quote: "Port of exit / Arrival date at port of entry / Addresses - bit more complex this. Check your answers, and Overview page, and the page itself should be [Section heading] Addresses [H1] Consignment addresses [Validation] Complete consignment addresses". What the quote says in so many words is verbatim; what it only implies (the rejected alternatives "Exit border control post" and "Arrival date at destination", the plants mirroring, the section numbers and the overview hint staying, and the exit port and arrival date wording applying beyond check your answers) is inferred, with the statement naming what in the quote implies it.

Anything the ruling touches but leaves open, as a gap claim with an empty quote — for example that the quote names no page, component or repo path for these wordings, and gives no wording for any other review-page duplication.

ref on every claim naming the file and the list item, such as "ruling-sam-2026-11-17.md claim 2" or "ruling-sam-2026-11-17.md claim 3 bullet 3"; note on each saying which report question and conflict it answers, or that it is new.
